metadata.case_name: NG KAM CHIU v. LAI YAT HUNG AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: Student (Form 5 at the Christian Faith College, Kowloon City)
plaintiff.occupation_after: Examiner in a watch factory; Driver of a dual-purpose van

injuries.description: laceration to the head resulting in a one inch scar
source: an injury to the head was also mentioned in the reports from the hospital doctors this appears to have consisted solely of a laceration which was subsequently not mentioned by the plaintiff when he gave evidence and the resulting one inch scar was described by Dr. Wedderburn in his report as "not conspicuous".
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: severe comminuted fracture of the head of the left femur
source: the principal injury sustained by the plaintiff was a severe comminuted fracture of the head of the left femur.

injuries.description: destruction of joint cartilage of the hip joint with prosthesis impinging on bone of the hip joint socket
source: this almost certainly means that there has been destruction of joint cartilage so that the prosthesis is now impinging directly on the bone of the hip joint socket without the normal cushion of the joint cartilage.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the hip or thigh

manifestations.description: one inch scar on head (not conspicuous)
mild impairment of strength of his left leg
increasing pain in the region of his hip, particularly after walking for 15 minutes or less
reduced walking tolerance (previously could walk half an hour; now discomfort after 15 minutes or less)
cannot run without difficulty and pain
unable to play any sports at all

treatments_received: Austin Moore Arthroplasty (replacement of the head and neck of the femur) performed on 25th October 1983
transfer from Queen Elizabeth Hospital to Kowloon Hospital for convalescence on 2nd November 1983
treatments_future: further operation to insert a prosthesis into the hip joint socket

losses.description: one inch scar on head (not conspicuous)

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: As a result of his injuries he is now not able to play any sports at all, and he cannot now run without difficulty and pain.
reduced walking tolerance; increasing pain after walking for 15 minutes or less; difficulty climbing/walking up slopes when repeated

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education

losses.description: earning capacity diminished; severe disadvantage in seeking employment and difficulty in finding employment as a result of his injuries

comparable_cases.case_name: Yang Yi Chai v. Chang Kan Shing and Tsui Tsz Choi
comparable_cases.injury_description: 70-year-old plaintiff who had an identical operation as in this case
